tasks.title: Set up Supabase database schema and PostGIS extension
tasks.description: Create all required database tables (lighting_points, incidents, overlast_zones, unsafe_areas, buurt_baseline, safety_grid) with PostGIS support for geospatial queries
tasks.details:
1. Enable PostGIS extension in Supabase
2. Create migration for all 6 tables per PRD schema
3. Add indexes on (lat, lng) columns and grid_x/grid_y
4. Create GiST indexes on geometry columns (unsafe_areas.geometry, overlast_zones.geometry)
5. Verify foreign key relationship between safety_grid.buurt_code and buurt_baseline.buurt_code
6. Test with sample inserts to validate geometry columns accept GeoJSON

Key columns:
- lighting_points: id (uuid), lat, lng, type, imported_at
- incidents: id (uuid), lat, lng, category, occurred_at, imported_at
- overlast_zones: id (uuid), kind, geometry (jsonb), validity_days (text[]), validity_hours, polarity
- unsafe_areas: id (uuid), name, kind, source, geometry (jsonb)
- buurt_baseline: buurt_code (text, PK), veiligheidsindex (float), updated_at
- safety_grid: id (uuid), grid_x, grid_y, lat, lng, buurt_code, lighting_score, incident_score, building_density_score, overview_score, camera_bonus, overlast_penalty, hotspot_penalty, updated_at
tasks.testStrategy: Run migration script and verify all tables exist with correct schema using `supabase db diff`. Insert test records with sample GeoJSON geometries and verify they're stored correctly. Query with PostGIS functions (ST_Contains, ST_Distance) to validate spatial indexing works.

tasks.title: Build Amsterdam Data API client and data import pipeline
tasks.description: Create Python module to fetch data from Amsterdam Data API endpoints and populate database tables
tasks.details:
1. Add `httpx` and `anthropic` to requirements.txt (already has httpx)
2. Create `backend/services/amsterdam_api.py` with async client for:
   - `/v1/leidingeninfrastructuur/amsterdam_ovl_lichtpunten` → lighting_points
   - `/v1/meldingen` (filter categories, last 24 months) → incidents
   - `/v1/overlastgebieden` → overlast_zones
   - `/v1/bag` → building density aggregation
   - `/v1/gebieden` → buurt boundaries for baseline join
   - `/v1/functionele_gebieden` → park polygons for unsafe_areas
3. Implement pagination handling and rate limiting
4. Create `backend/scripts/import_data.py` CLI to run full import
5. Store API key in .env as `AMSTERDAM_DATA_API_KEY`
6. Parse time validity from overlast_zones (validity_days, validity_hours)
7. Geocode unsafe_areas from survey Tables 1, §1.7, §1.8 (hardcoded seed data)

API client should handle:
- Authentication via API key header
- Retry logic with exponential backoff
- GeoJSON geometry transformation to JSONB
- Filtering meldingen to relevant categories: 'overlast-personen-groepen', 'overlast-op-het-water', etc.
tasks.testStrategy: Mock Amsterdam Data API responses and verify parsing logic. Run import script against live API (with small limit) and verify records appear in database. Validate geometry fields contain valid GeoJSON. Check that overlast_zones polarity is set correctly (cameratoezicht = bonus, others = penalty).

tasks.title: Implement safety_grid pre-computation and scoring model
tasks.description: Build grid generation logic and compute static safety layer scores per 100m cell
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/services/grid_builder.py`
2. Generate ~100m grid cells covering Amsterdam bounding box (52.27–52.43 N, 4.73–5.08 E)
3. For each cell, compute:
   - lighting_score: density of lichtpunten within 100m radius, normalized 0–1
   - incident_score: inverted density of meldingen (last 24 months) within 100m, normalized 0–1
   - building_density_score: BAG residential + non-residential count within cell, normalized 0–1
   - overview_score: 1.0 minus coverage by dense parks/tunnels (use functionele_gebieden)
   - camera_bonus: 0–0.2 if cell overlaps cameratoezicht zones
   - overlast_penalty: 0–0.3 sum of overlapping overlastgebieden (excluding cameratoezicht)
   - hotspot_penalty: 0–0.2 if cell overlaps unsafe_areas polygons
4. Join buurt_code from gebieden polygons using PostGIS ST_Contains
5. Store results in safety_grid table
6. Create `backend/services/scorer.py` with time-of-day weight tables per PRD

Time-of-day weights (day/evening/night):
- people_density: 0.22/0.20/0.18
- overview: 0.16/0.18/0.20
- lighting: 0.14/0.20/0.26
- building_density: 0.18/0.14/0.10
- camera_bonus: 0.04/0.06/0.08
- overlast_penalty: 0.08/0.14/0.18
- incidents: 0.10/0.10/0.10
- hotspot_penalty: 0.08/0.12/0.16
tasks.testStrategy: Generate grid for small test area (e.g., Centrum district only). Verify cell count and coverage. Spot-check cells near known landmarks (Vondelpark, Leidseplein) have expected penalty scores. Validate that scores are within 0–1 range. Test time-of-day weight application returns different scores for same cell at different times.

tasks.title: Integrate Google Maps Directions API for route fetching
tasks.description: Create service to fetch cycling and walking route alternatives from Google Maps Directions API
tasks.details:
1. Add `googlemaps` Python library to requirements.txt
2. Create `backend/services/directions.py` with:
   - `fetch_route_alternatives(origin, destination, mode, departure_time)` returning up to 3 routes
   - Mode: 'bicycling' or 'walking'
   - Parse response to extract: encoded polyline, distance_m, duration_min
3. Store `GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` in backend/.env
4. Decode polyline to lat/lng coordinate list using `polyline` library
5. Handle errors: no routes found, API quota exceeded, invalid addresses
6. Return structured RouteAlternative objects with polyline, distance, duration

Google Directions API request:
- origin/destination: address strings or lat,lng
- mode: bicycling | walking
- departure_time: Unix timestamp (for time-of-day routing)
- alternatives: true (request up to 3 routes)
- region: nl
- language: nl
tasks.testStrategy: Mock Google API responses with 3 route alternatives. Verify polyline decoding produces valid coordinate sequences. Test error handling for invalid addresses, no routes found. Validate that departure_time parameter is passed correctly.

tasks.title: Build route scoring and selection algorithm
tasks.description: Score each route alternative using safety_grid and select the safest route
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/services/route_scorer.py`
2. Implement `score_route(polyline_coords, departure_time)` that:
   - Samples polyline at regular intervals (~50m)
   - Looks up nearest safety_grid cell for each sample point
   - Computes people_density_score from crowdmonitor + heuristic based on departure_time
   - Applies time-of-day weights per PRD (day: 06–20, evening: 20–23, night: 23–06)
   - Calculates per-cell score: veiligheidsindex_buurt × weighted sum of layer scores
   - Returns mean cell score scaled 0–10
3. Implement hotspot detection: identify which unsafe_area polygons the route intersects
4. Return RouteScore object with: total_score, hotspots_passed, cell_scores[]
5. In `GET /routes` endpoint, score all alternatives and return highest-scoring route

People density heuristic (when crowdmonitor data missing):
- Residential streets: 0.3 day, 0.5 evening, 0.1 night
- Commercial streets: 0.7 day, 0.6 evening, 0.2 night
- Parks/green: 0.4 day, 0.2 evening, 0.05 night
tasks.testStrategy: Create test routes (polylines) through high-safety and low-safety areas. Verify higher-safety route scores higher. Test time-of-day weighting changes scores appropriately (night emphasizes lighting more). Validate hotspot detection identifies unsafe_areas correctly. Score same route at different times and verify scores differ.

tasks.title: Set up Claude AI integration for route explanation and tips
tasks.description: Integrate Claude Sonnet 4.6 API to generate plain-language route explanations and contextual safety tips
tasks.details:
1. Add `anthropic` SDK to requirements.txt
2. Create `backend/services/ai_narrator.py` with:
   - `generate_explanation(route_data, score_breakdown)` → 2–3 sentence explanation
   - `generate_tips(route_data, hotspots, time, mode)` → 3–5 contextual tips
3. System prompt with PRD context, survey stats, and instruction to be concise and grounding
4. Use prompt caching on system prompt (cache_control header)
5. Input to Claude: polyline summary, crossed grid cells, layer subscores, departure_time, mode, hotspots_passed
6. Hard timeout 2s; on failure return ai_status: "fallback" and static tips
7. Store `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in backend/.env
8. Use model `claude-sonnet-4-6-20250929`

Static fallback tips:
- "Stay aware of your surroundings and trust your instincts"
- "Share your live location with a friend before leaving"
- "Have your phone charged and accessible"
- "Stick to well-lit main roads when possible"
- "If you feel unsafe, enter a 24h business or call 112"

Tip triggers:
- Passing park after sunset → "Parks are less safe at night; stay on main paths"
- Passing station → "Train stations can be busy; keep valuables secure"
- Passing nightlife square → "This area has nightlife activity; stay alert"
- Walking mode at night → "Consider cycling for faster, safer travel"
tasks.testStrategy: Mock Anthropic API responses and verify parsing. Test timeout handling returns fallback. Verify prompt includes all required context (route summary, scores, time, mode). Test tip generation with different hotspot combinations. Validate ai_status field is set correctly (ok vs fallback).

tasks.title: Implement FastAPI backend routes (/routes, /safety, /tips)
tasks.description: Build REST API endpoints per PRD specification
tasks.details:
1. Create `backend/routers/routes.py` with:
   - `GET /routes?from={address}&to={address}&time={iso_timestamp}&mode={cycling|walking}`
   - Geocode addresses using Google Geocoding API
   - Fetch route alternatives from directions service
   - Score routes and select best
   - Generate AI explanation and tips (with fallback)
   - Return JSON per PRD schema: {route: {polyline, distance_m, duration_min, hotspots_passed}, explanation, tips, ai_status}
2. Create `GET /safety?lat={lat}&lng={lng}&radius={m}&time={iso_timestamp}`
   - Return safety score for location at given time (debug endpoint)
3. Create `GET /tips?time={iso_timestamp}&mode={mode}&hotspots={comma_separated}`
   - Regenerate tips without re-routing (for client time changes)
4. Add response models using Pydantic
5. Handle errors: invalid params, geocoding failures, no routes found
6. Register routers in main.py

Response schema (GET /routes):
```json
{
  "route": {
    "polyline": "encoded_string",
    "distance_m": 2400,
    "duration_min": 12,
    "hotspots_passed": ["park", "station"]
  },
  "explanation": "This route avoids...",
  "tips": ["..."],
  "ai_status": "ok" | "fallback"
}
```
tasks.testStrategy: Test each endpoint with valid and invalid parameters. Verify error responses are properly formatted. Test geocoding with real Amsterdam addresses. Mock scoring service and verify correct route is selected. Test ai_status fallback when AI service fails. Validate response matches PRD JSON schema.

tasks.title: Build frontend route input form with address autocomplete
tasks.description: Create React component for route input with Google Places Autocomplete
tasks.details:
1. Install `@react-google-maps/api` in frontend
2. Create `frontend/components/RouteForm.tsx` with:
   - Start address input with Google Places Autocomplete (bias to Amsterdam)
   - Destination address input with autocomplete
   - Departure time picker (defaults to now, allows future selection)
   - Mode selector (cycling / walking radio buttons)
   - Submit button
3. Use `@react-google-maps/api` LoadScript and Autocomplete components
4. Store `NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` in frontend/.env.local
5. Validate inputs before submit: both addresses required, time not in past
6. On submit, call `POST /routes` via frontend/lib/api.ts
7. Show loading state during API call
8. Style with Tailwind CSS 4 (use design tokens, avoid hardcoded colors)

Form fields:
- Start: text input with autocomplete, placeholder "Start address"
- Destination: text input with autocomplete, placeholder "Destination address"
- Departure time: datetime-local input, default to now
- Mode: radio group, options "Cycling" / "Walking", default "Cycling"
- Submit: button "Find safest route"
tasks.testStrategy: Test autocomplete suggests Amsterdam addresses. Verify form validation prevents submission with empty fields or past time. Mock API response and verify loading state appears. Test error handling when API fails. Validate form works on mobile viewport.

tasks.title: Build route display component with Google Maps integration
tasks.description: Create component to display selected route on map with explanation and tips
tasks.details:
1. Create `frontend/components/RouteDisplay.tsx` using `@react-google-maps/api`
2. Display Google Map centered on route with:
   - Polyline overlay (decode from API response)
   - Start and destination markers
   - Hotspot markers (parks, stations, squares) along route
3. Show route metadata card:
   - Distance (km)
   - Estimated travel time
   - AI-generated explanation
4. Display contextual tips list (3–5 items)
5. "Open in Google Maps" button:
   - Generate deep link: `https://www.google.com/maps/dir/?api=1&origin={start}&destination={dest}&travelmode={mode}`
   - Opens in new tab
6. Handle ai_status: "fallback" → show warning "Tips generated from fallback data"
7. Responsive design: map above on mobile, side-by-side on desktop

Map configuration:
- Default zoom: fit route bounds
- Map style: clean, minimal (no extra POIs)
- Controls: zoom, but no street view or satellite toggle
tasks.testStrategy: Mock route response and verify map renders with polyline. Test marker placement at correct coordinates. Verify "Open in Google Maps" link has correct parameters and opens. Test responsive layout on mobile and desktop. Validate ai_status warning appears when status is "fallback".

tasks.title: Create landing page with problem statement and survey stats

tasks.details:
1. Update `frontend/app/page.tsx` with:
   - Hero section: "Starlight — Safe Routes for Women in Amsterdam"
   - Problem statement: "78% of young women have felt afraid cycling in Amsterdam at night. Starlight helps you find the safest route."

2. Footer with:

   - "Data sources" link to /about page
   - Hackathon attribution
3. Style with Tailwind CSS 4
4. Ensure mobile-responsive
5. Add metadata for SEO: title, description, og:image

Key stats to highlight:
- 78% of young women have been afraid cycling
- 47% of adult cyclists fear harassment
- 50% already avoid certain routes
- Top request: better lighting and safer routes
tasks.testStrategy: Verify page renders all sections correctly. Test CTA button scrolls to form or navigates correctly. Validate footer links work. Test responsive design on mobile. Check metadata appears in page source.

tasks.title: Add time-of-day route comparison feature
tasks.description: Allow users to compare route safety at different times without re-entering addresses
tasks.details:
1. Update `RouteDisplay.tsx` to show time selector:
   - Quick picks: "Now", "Tonight (22:00)", "Late night (00:00)"
   - Custom time picker
2. When time changes, call `GET /tips?time={new_time}&mode={mode}&hotspots={hotspots}`
3. Update explanation and tips without re-rendering map
4. Show visual indicator when route score changes significantly (>15% difference)
5. Optional: show before/after score comparison (requires adding score to API response)

UI flow:
- User gets initial route for "now"
- Clicks "Tonight (22:00)" quick pick
- Tips update to show night-specific warnings
- Explanation regenerates with time-appropriate reasoning
tasks.testStrategy: Test time changes trigger tips refresh. Verify map and route metadata don't re-render unnecessarily. Mock API responses for different times and verify tips change appropriately. Test quick picks set correct times. Validate custom time picker works.

tasks.title: End-to-end testing and production deployment validation
tasks.description: Test full user flow, deploy to production, and validate with real data
tasks.details:
1. Run full data import for Amsterdam (lighting, incidents, overlast zones, BAG, etc.)
2. Generate complete safety_grid for Amsterdam
3. Test full user flow:
   - Enter real Amsterdam addresses (e.g., Centraal Station → Vondelpark)
   - Verify route is returned in <5s
   - Check explanation is coherent and grounded
   - Verify tips are contextual to route
   - Test "Open in Google Maps" launches correctly
4. Deploy backend to Railway, frontend to Vercel
5. Set production environment variables
6. Test production deployment with real addresses
7. Monitor API latency and error rates
8. Verify CORS allows Vercel domain
9. Test on mobile devices (iOS Safari, Android Chrome)
10. Load test with 10 concurrent users

Production checklist:
- All data layers imported and grid computed
- Environment variables set in Railway and Vercel
- CORS configured for production domains
- API keys valid and have sufficient quota
- Anthropic API prompt caching enabled
- Error monitoring configured
- Mobile responsive design validated
tasks.testStrategy: Full regression test suite covering happy path and error cases. Load testing to verify <5s p95 latency. Cross-browser and mobile device testing. Production smoke test after deployment. Monitor error logs for 24 hours post-deployment.
